root_cause.ad991b299cf05589d: Every load-bearing fact is restated in six to ten places with no canonical copy — the L02/L08 fate lives in the report's front-matter summary, §3, §10, the session card's banner AND its item 4, and the CONTRACTS EXTERNAL log, and was corrected in rounds 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16 and is still flagged in 17; the B5-provenance guarantee sat in the banner, §2 header, findings README, workflows README and session card (rounds 9-11); the phrase 'same rule as Fleet A' sat in four places across 05-eap-false-done-ledger.js (meta.phases, the dies() comment, the Phase-3 heading) and workflows/README.md and took rounds 11-14 to purge, so 13 of the 36 findings in rounds 10-17 are pure propagation residue of the previous fix. Each fix commit also writes fresh prose — new diagnoses, citations, labels and a growing EXTERNAL tally line — instead of deleting duplicates, so fixes become the next round's targets: 8 of the 18 substantive findings in this range were introduced by an earlier fix commit (the B14 claim by round 9; the 04/05 divergence, isNegativeCoverage gap and the L02-superbot attribution by round 1's 76834c8; 'real, distinct measurement' by round 11; the 'not re-citable' citation and OWNER mislabels by round 13; the 'extraction inconsistency' diagnosis by round 14; the :171→:182 shift by round 15). Underneath that, the §2 rows were drafted from candidate headline text while the header promised the verifier's corrected_claim, so the retained JSON already contained the refutation of three core rows (result.verified[8], [10] and [0] discrepancies) — Codex kept finding errors simply by reading the raw JSON the report summarized, and those original-draft errors (rounds 11, 13, 14) are what a 3-round cap would have merged. Finally, patching 05 mid-review under a verbatim-as-run convention that left 04 untouched manufactured a real executable divergence that then had to be described consistently in four more places.
root_cause.ab98baa07215c0bf6: The PR restates the same handful of facts in at least five files and roughly a dozen locations: inside the report each claim appears in the front-matter banner, the §0 executive summary, the §2/§3 rows, a §4 heading and a §5 closing note, and the same claims are re-rendered in the session card (Status block and Report section), the docs/findings/README.md index row, docs/findings/data/workflows/README.md, and four lines of 05-CONTRACTS-night.md (AGGREGATE, RETAIN, CORPUS, EXTERNAL) — 'critics reproduced in full' lived in four files and took rounds 1, 2/3 and 4 to clear, 'unanimous' took rounds 2, 3 and 4, and the 'corrected_claim-only' guarantee took rounds 6, 7, 8 and 9. Each fix commit touched only a subset of those copies, and because every Codex round reviews the previous fix commit's head, the residue plus any new sentence the fix itself introduced (76834c8's 'general knowledge' line and mis-written fixture tally, 1965aa9's 'failure count is unknown', fa16a99's 'readers never opened' and its wrong README provenance for B5) became the next round's findings — 16 of the 52 threads in rounds 1-9 are of this kind. The live round/finding tally embedded in the report note, session card, findings index and CONTRACTS sheet was stale by construction (the commit that fixes round N is exactly what round N+1 reviews) and produced a finding in each of rounds 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 until fee0e4b/fa16a99 reduced it to one location. Underneath that churn the original report carried genuine core errors that Codex surfaced only incrementally — judge scores and FD-01 independence in round 2, survivor #12's un-applied narrowing in round 4, the 10-vs-9 misattribution (94af16e:89-91) in round 7, and the L02→FD-09 mapping (94af16e:281) not until round 9 — so rounds 4, 7 and 9 each corrected a core claim a 3-round cap would have shipped, and the self-inflicted loop is also what kept the reviewer looking long enough to find them.
